newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan sets revamped BCCI unit sale for June 12.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan sets revamped BCCI unit sale for June 12.

text.p: Pakistan's state Privatisation Commission said on Wednesday it would hold final bidding on June 12 to sell 70 percent shares of a revamped unit of the former Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI).
The bidding for Habib Credit and Exchange Bank Ltd (HCEBL), formed in 1992 from three BCCI branches in Pakistan, will be shown live on state television, a Commission official said.
The deal is expected to fetch $50 million, Commission sources said.

HCEBL, a susidiary of the Habib Bank Limited, will be the third bank to be privatised by Pakistan after the transfer of the controlling shares of the Muslim Commercial Bank to a private group and of the Allied Bank Ltd to its employees.
Its accounts for the year ended December 31, 1996, showed a five percent growth in net profit over the 1995 profit of 265 million rupees.

Nine foreign and local companies are in the field for bidding for HCEBL's 70 percent shares, commission sources said. The government will retain 20 percent shares and 10 percent will be offered to the bank's employees.
